resources.string: Taps and drags go where your finger is.

The screen works as a laptop touchpad: tap to click, two-finger tap for right click, three-finger tap for middle click, two-finger drag to scroll, double-tap and drag to hold the button. Speed and tapping follow the desktop\'s touchpad settings.
A mouse or touchpad always moves the pointer directly.
The desktop takes this window\'s size, like a monitor: rotating or opening the keyboard resizes it.
Copy on one side, paste on the other. Android\'s copies arrive when Chameleon is in front.

Android keeps some shortcuts, like Alt+Tab and Meta, for itself. Turn on \"Chameleon keyboard shortcuts\" in Accessibility to send them to the desktop. If it is greyed out, allow restricted settings in Chameleon\'s App info menu first.

While Chameleon is in front, sends every key of a hardware keyboard to the desktop, including shortcuts Android keeps for itself (Alt+Tab, Meta…). Volume and power keys stay with Android. Nothing is read or sent while another app is in front.
